episode_title: From 2 Suitcases To 29 Flips In 7 Years (Case Study)
question: How much did Matt Burks make on his first house flip in New Zealand and how long did the project take?
transcript_excerpt: Matt cleared approximately $100,000 on his first flip. The renovation took about six weeks to two months, with the entire project including sale completed in about three months. He initially planned to hold it as a rental but realized he had no money to do so and no job to support bank refinancing, so he sold it instead.

episode_title: From 2 Suitcases To 29 Flips In 7 Years (Case Study)
question: What was Matt Burks' smelliest property purchase and how much profit did he make from the auction sale?
transcript_excerpt: Matt bought a severely damaged property with a tarped roof for $90,000 on December 20th with virtually no renovation budget. He cleaned up the backyard for $3,000 and took it to auction with a $150,000 reserve. The property sold for $315,000, setting his entire property career up. He attributes part of the success to including a survey showing subdivision potential.

episode_title: From 2 Suitcases To 29 Flips In 7 Years (Case Study)
question: How much money did Matt Burks lose on his first property development project with KO?
transcript_excerpt: Matt lost a couple of hundred thousand dollars on his first development deal. KO agreed to buy the properties but later requested a price adjustment, forcing Matt to fund the difference at a discounted rate. Rather than continue losing money on the project, he signed at the lower price to exit the deal, recognizing that taking a loss was better than remaining tied to a failing project.

episode_title: From 2 Suitcases To 29 Flips In 7 Years (Case Study)
question: How much did Matt Burks' property investment mentorship course cost in New Zealand?
transcript_excerpt: The mentorship course cost approximately $35,000 to $40,000. Matt saved the money while working for his father and living at home from age 15 to 21, supplemented by putting some costs on a credit card before selling a property in Australia to clear it. The course taught him how to buy a house and make money, with a claimed 95% success rate of participants actually buying something.

episode_title: From 2 Suitcases To 29 Flips In 7 Years (Case Study)
question: How many rental properties does Matt Burks currently own and how many is he planning to build?
transcript_excerpt: Matt currently owns seven rental properties, none of which are from his 29 flips. He is about to build another five new properties and has a large 12,000-square development site where he lives that he plans to develop into rentals. He also has a couple of other smaller projects in the works.

episode_title: From 2 Suitcases To 29 Flips In 7 Years (Case Study)
question: What was the starting capital Matt Burks had when moving to New Zealand and how did he finance the property course?
transcript_excerpt: Matt arrived with $30,000 in his bank account and two Australian credit cards with $9,000 and $16,000 available limits respectively, totaling $55,000 in accessible funds. He had accumulated savings from working for his father since leaving school at age 15, which he used for the $35,000-$40,000 property course, supplementing it with credit card borrowing.
